clues.title: Coverage: Pacific islands counted as the US
text: **American Samoa** is a group of islands east of Fiji, located in the Pacific Ocean. Since it is a US overseas territory, for country streak purposes, it is counted as the US.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A group of Pacific islands east of Fiji. It is a US territory, so for country streaks it counts as the US.

clues.title: Landscape: green mountains, palms, tin roofs
text: The general landscape consists of **green, tropical** mountains with many palm trees. Small roads are often made of [concrete](https://goo.gl/maps/GENv4jmjUzvkSbp38). Most houses are one storey, and have a simple box design. Plain **metal sheet** roofs are also very common.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Green tropical mountains with many palm trees. Small roads are often concrete, houses are one-storey boxes, and plain metal sheet roofs are common.

clues.title: Google car: rusted black truck bed
text: A slightly **rusted black** truck bed can be seen on the main island of Tutuila.
This is the most common car that will be seen as it has the most coverage.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A slightly rusted black truck bed is visible. It is the most common car, because the main island has the most coverage.

clues.title: Google car: silver-grey truck front, side mirrors
text: The front of a **silver-grey** truck with side mirrors can be seen on Manu’a and Olosega, which are connected by a bridge.
_See below for more information._

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: You see the front of a silver-grey truck with its side mirrors. It covers two islands joined by a bridge.

clues.title: Google car: glossy black truck front
text: The front of a similar truck can be seen on the easternmost covered island of Tau. However, the truck will be **glossy black**, with side mirrors visible.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Like the silver-grey truck but glossy black, with side mirrors visible. It covers the easternmost covered island.

clues.title: Bridge: single lane, thin wire guardrail
text: The **single-lane** bridge, connecting the islands of Manu’a and Olosega, can be easily recognized by the thin wire guardrail, with the two islands on either side of the bridge.

images.caption: Single-lane bridge with a thin wire guardrail

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A one-lane bridge between two islands with a thin wire guardrail, and an island on each side.

clues.title: Airport: small concrete runway, orange straps
text: Ofu Airport is small with a **concrete** runway. The Google Car covering it has two **orange straps** on the roof. Many palm trees can also be seen on the other side of the runway.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A small airport with a concrete runway and many palms across it. The car has two orange straps on its roof.

clues.title: Road: urban north-south road, mountain north
text: The Rte 018 in Tafuna is **urban** and uniquely shows this **mountain in the North**. The alignment is generally **North-South**. The road has **double yellow lines** (not that common in AS) and a **power line in the East**. The driving direction is to the **North**.

Make sure that parts of the Rte 001 can look similar with a similar road angle. To confirm it's the Rte 018, you can pan exactly North. If you look at the mountain, it's the Rte 018, otherwise it's not.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Urban road running north-south, driving north, with a mountain ahead, double yellow lines and a power line to the east. Panning exactly north should show that mountain.

clues.title: Town: coast to the north, mountains elsewhere
text: Faleasao is a little town on Tau (and thus has the **Tau car**). It has a **coast in the North** and is otherwise surrounded by **mountains**. Together with the Tau car, it is unique.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A small town on the easternmost island, so the glossy black truck. The sea lies to the north and mountains surround it everywhere else.

clues.title: Road: north coast next to the bridge, paved
text: On Manu'a/Olosega (which have a unique car), there are two covered roads with **North coast**: The roads east and west of the famous bridge. They can easily be differentiated, because the Olosega (east) road is **unpaved**, while the Manu'a (west) road has **concrete pavement**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Two covered roads with a north coast lie either side of the bridge. The west one has concrete pavement; the east one is unpaved.

clues.title: Road: south coast, driving west
text: This long stretch of road (which is probably further regionguessable) is easily recognizable because it has a **South Coast** and the Car Drives **westward** (unlike the Western Coastal Road). That means that when you pan onto the back of the truck, the water will be to your right .
There is one annoying exception, around the POI 'Amouli Beach Fales' east of the town Amouli.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A long road with the sea to the south, driving west. Pan to the back of the truck and the water is on your right. One exception near a beach resort.

clues.title: Road: odd angle, mountains north, summit west
text: This road crosses the district border on the 001. It is characterized through the **unique angle** and the **mountains in the north**. Often you can see a unique summit in the west. The driving direction is **eastwards**.
There is a stretch of the 001 with a similar angle near Malaeimi, but it has a clearly visible valley in the North which is not found on this road.
The road can further be divided as it is **overcast** in the Western District and **sunny** in the Eastern District.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A main-road stretch crossing a district border, driving east at a distinctive angle with mountains north and often a unique summit in the west. West part is overcast, east part sunny.

clues.title: Landscape: very urban, harbour in view
text: The roads alonog the Pago Pago Harbour are recognizable because they're generally **very urban** (for American Samoa), and you can often see the **harbour** when it isn't blocked by buildings.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Roads around a harbour are the most urban in the territory, and you can often see the water between buildings.

clues.title: Road: the straightest road, very flat
text: This section of the Rte 014 is by far the **straightest** covered road on Tutuila. Use the road angle to confirm. The appearance is quite varied, but it's also very flat

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A section of Route 014 that is by far the straightest covered road on the main island. Check the road angle. Looks varied but is very flat.

clues.title: Roadside: airport fences
text: On the roads along the airport on Tutuila, you will always see these **fences** surrounding the airport. This is obviously common for airports, but since Tutuila only has one airstrip, this road is a free 5k together with the Tutuila car.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Fences surround the airport along the road. The main island has only one airstrip, so this is an easy pin with its truck.

clues.title: Road: south coast, driving east
text: This road is easily recognizable because it has a **South Coast** and the Car drives **eastward** (unlike the Eastern Coastal Road). That means that when you pan onto the back of the truck, the water will be to your left .
On the eastern south coast road, there is a tiny part that also drives eastward for some reason, which can be baity.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A road with the sea to the south, driving east. Pan to the back of the truck and the water is on your left. A tiny part of the other south-coast road also drives east, which can trick you.

clues.title: Road: plain sand road, no grass strip
text: From slightly North of the town entry of Olosega until the southernmost house WEST of the road, you will have a plain sand road, with no grass verge in the middle.
This is the only road of this kind on the two islands with this Google Car.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Starting just north of the town entrance until the southernmost house west of the road, the road is plain sand with no grass strip in the middle. Only road like it on the two islands with this car.

clues.title: Beach: sea to the south-east, three peaks
text: Ofu Beach is easy to recognize, with the coast to the Southeast and three distinct peaks in the Northeast.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Walker coverage on a beach with the coast to the south-east and three distinct peaks in the north-east.

clues.title: Bay: opens to the north-east
text: Vatia Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards Northeast. Note that Fagasa Bay is opened towards Northwest, while Afono Bay is opened towards North proper.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: The only covered bay opening to the north-east. Another bay opens north-west, and a third opens due north.

clues.title: Town: west coast, fully paved, no mountain north
text: The town Ofu on Manu'a has a West Coast. This road can be distinguished from the West Coast of Olosega, because:
It is entirely paved (unlike the town Olosega)
It has no Mountain in the North (unlike the paved road north of Olosega).

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A town with a west coast. Unlike the neighbouring island's town it is entirely paved, and there is no mountain to the north.

clues.title: Road: concrete road with no coast, far east
text: If you are on Tutuila and have a Concrete Road with no coast visible, you're on the far Eastern Part of the island, between Onenoa and Matatula Elementary school.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: On the main island, a concrete road with no coast in view means the far east, between two villages near a school.

clues.title: Bay: opens due north
text: Afono Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards straight North. Note that Fagasa Bay is opened towards Northwest, while Vatia Bay is opened towards Northeast.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: The only covered bay opening straight north. Another opens north-west and a third north-east.

clues.title: Road: east-west asphalt, far west end
text: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
If you're generally heading East-West and have Asphalt pavement, you're on the far west part of the road.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: A long east-west road on the easternmost island is hard to line up. Heading east-west on asphalt puts you at its far western end.

clues.title: Road: concrete, overgrown, no guardrail
text: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and a lot of overgrowth between you and the coast, you're generally in the Western Part of the road.
If additionally, you have **no guardrail**, you're on the stretch marked on the second image, south of a smooth coast protrusion west of the river.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: On the long east-west road, concrete, plenty of overgrowth towards the coast and no guardrail means the western part, south of a smooth coastal bump west of the river.

clues.title: Road: concrete, overgrown, power line
text: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and a lot of overgrowth between you and the coast, you're generally in the Western Part of the road.
If additionally, you have a powerline visible, you're on the SW-NE stretch immediately west of the river.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: On the long east-west road, concrete, overgrowth towards the coast and a visible power line mean the stretch just west of the river that runs south-west to north-east.

clues.title: Road: concrete, coconut palms, power line
text: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you see a lot of Coconut Palms, you're in the central part of the road, east of the river.
The short stretch immediately east of the river only shows the Coconuts in the distance towards East. There's both a Powerline and a Guardrail.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: On the long east-west road, concrete with lots of coconut palms puts you in the middle, east of the river. Just east of the river: palms in the distance, a power line and a guardrail.

clues.title: Road: concrete, coconuts, power line, no guardrail
text: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you see a lot of Coconut Palms, you're in the central part of the road, east of the river.
On this stretch, if you have a powerline, but no guardrail, you're east of the river, and west of the small sideroad on the map.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: On the long east-west road, concrete with many coconut palms, a power line but no guardrail puts you east of the river and west of the small side road.

clues.title: Road: concrete, coconuts, no power line
text: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you see a lot of Coconut Palms, you're in the central part of the road, east of the river.
The short stretch immediately east of the little sideroad has no powerline, unlike the other locs with Coconuts.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: On the long east-west road, concrete and many coconut palms, but no power line, means the short stretch just east of the small side road.

clues.title: Road: concrete, open coast north, guardrail
text: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you have the coast North of you, with no significant vegetation in the way, you're on the Easternmost part of the road, east of the little sideroad.
The western half of this stretch has a guardrail, the eastern half does not.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: On the long east-west road, concrete with the sea open to the north means the easternmost part. The western half of this stretch has a guardrail.

clues.title: Landscape: two small peaks reaching into the sea
text: Behold: The Camel Rock. Two little peaks reaching into the ocean.
It is marked as a POI on Google Maps.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Two little peaks sticking out into the ocean, known as Camel Rock. It is marked as a point of interest on Google Maps.

clues.title: Road: concrete, overgrown, guardrail
text: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and a lot of overgrowth between you and the coast, you're generally in the Western Part of the road.
If additionally, you have a guardrail, but no powerline, you're on the east-west stretch west of the river.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: On the long east-west road, concrete, overgrowth towards the coast and a guardrail but no power line means the stretch west of the river.

clues.title: Coast: sea to the east, nothing else in view
text: This is the only part of Tutuila where you can see Coast on the east, without other parts of Tutuila visible. You will often see Aunu'u in the Southeast.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: The only place on the main island where the coast is to the east without other parts of the island visible. A small island is often visible to the south-east.

clues.title: Bay: opens to the north-west
text: Afono Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards Northwest. Note that Afono is opened towards North proper, while Vatia Bay is opened towards Northeast.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: The only covered bay opening to the north-west. Another bay opens due north, and a third opens north-east.

text: The only ferry Trekker of American Samoa. If you're on a boat between two islands in AS, you're here.

clues.summary: This is the only ferry coverage in the territory. If you are on a boat between two islands, you are here.
